issue: Does the 'reasonable belief' standard that permits police to enter a third party's home to arrest a suspect require probable cause, or is it a lesser standard?

sides.position: Reasonable belief amounts to probable cause.
cases: United States v. Barrera, 464 F.3d 496 (5th Cir. 2006)
United States v. Hardin, 539 F.3d 404 (6th Cir. 2008)
United States v. Gorman, 314 F.3d 1105 (9th Cir. 2002)
United States v. Magluta, 44 F.3d 1530 (11th Cir. 1995)

sides.position: Reasonable belief requires something less than probable cause.
cases: United States v. Lauter, 57 F.3d 212 (2d Cir. 1995)
United States v. Thomas, 429 F.3d 282 (D.C. Cir. 2005)

quote: Our sister circuits are split as to the definition of “reasonable belief.”
cite: United States v. Justin Thabit, 56 F.4th 1145 (8th Cir. 2023)
